title: The Sheriff, the Governor, and the Vanishing Endorsement
excerpt: A message attributed to Sheriff Martin Cuellar asking Gov. Abbott to drop his endorsement is racing across Laredo social media. The message itself is unconfirmed — but the sheriff's name really did vanish from Abbott's list within hours.
content:
A message is racing across Laredo social media, attributed to Webb County Sheriff Martin Cuellar, asking Governor Greg Abbott to take the sheriff's name off an endorsement. Webb Watch 956 could not independently confirm the message is genuinely his — but this much is documented: within hours of Abbott announcing Cuellar as one of 12 Democratic sheriffs backing his re-election on Monday, the campaign's endorsement page listed only 11 names. The sheriff's was gone, and the campaign offered no explanation.

The screenshot, shared widely by the local page 24/7 Laredo on Monday, shows a post attributed to Cuellar reading, in part: "Please remove my name from this endorsement for the governor... This is sheriff martin Cuellar. The governor endorsed tano my brother's opponent. Thank you."

What is verified

The endorsement and the disappearance are real. On Monday, October 19 — the first day of early voting — Abbott announced endorsements from a slate of Democratic border sheriffs. The Texas Tribune and Hoodline reported that the campaign's list named 12 sheriffs, including Webb County's Martin Cuellar. The release posted on Abbott's campaign website, last updated at 11:45 a.m. Central on Monday, now lists 11 sheriffs and does not include Cuellar. The page does not explain the change, according to the Texas Gazette.

The family connection is real. Martin Cuellar is the brother of Democratic U.S. Representative Henry Cuellar of Laredo, who is fighting for re-election in Texas' 28th Congressional District against Webb County Judge Tano Tijerina. Abbott, like President Trump, has endorsed Tijerina in that race. The reason given in the attributed message — that the governor backed "my brother's opponent" — matches the public record.

The sheriff's legal situation is real. Martin Cuellar is under a five-count federal indictment returned in November 2025. Prosecutors allege that he and two former assistant chiefs used sheriff's office staff and resources to run a for-profit disinfecting company, Disinfect Pro Master, during the COVID-19 pandemic. Cuellar has pleaded not guilty, says he is innocent, and will fight the charges; his trial was pushed to February 2027. He is presumed innocent unless proven guilty, and the indictment is separate from the case against his brother, which ended in a presidential pardon in December 2025.

What Webb Watch could not confirm

Webb Watch 956 could not independently verify before publication that the screenshot shows a genuine post from Sheriff Cuellar's own account, and neither the Abbott campaign nor the sheriff's office had publicly explained the removal as of publication. Three explanations remain possible on the current record: the sheriff asked to be removed, as the attributed message states; he never agreed to endorse and was listed in error; or the campaign dropped an indicted official from a law-and-order rollout on its own. The documented facts — the listing, and then its quiet removal — fit the first explanation, but fitting is not confirming.

Why it matters in Webb County

The episode lands in the middle of the most contested congressional race in South Texas. Early voting runs through October 30, and Election Day is November 3. An endorsement page is a small thing; a sitting sheriff's name appearing on — and then vanishing from — a Republican governor's list, while that governor campaigns for the sheriff's brother's opponent, is not. Webb Watch 956 will update this story if the sheriff or the campaign confirms what happened.

Sources: Texas Gazette, "Abbott Touts Backing From Democratic Border Sheriffs as Voting Opens," Oct. 19, 2026; The Texas Tribune and Hoodline, via Texas Gazette; Reuters factbox on the Texas primaries, Mar. 3, 2026; KGNS reporting on the Martin Cuellar indictment; 24/7 Laredo social media post, Oct. 19, 2026.

— Walter Webb & Willa Webb, News Anchors, Webb Watch 956
